cue: Hold the phone still and let something move. A thin sharp strip of colour swings over to look at it.

fov.note: the side eyes between them cover almost the whole circle

cpd.note: the best measured side eye acuity, in an Evarcha

M.note: the side eyes hold one green pigment, so the wide picture carries one tone

gate.note: still things fade a good deal but stay faintly visible so the view can be read

living.note: extra weight for movement that looks alive

deg.note: one principal retina sees a strip about 2 degrees wide and 21 degrees tall

uv.note: ultraviolet drawn from the camera's blue and no red added

saccade.note: a 15 degree jump takes at most 0.1 second

sweep.note: side to side across the target; the app's rounding of the measured scan

twist.note: degrees each way, milliseconds to turn, milliseconds held at each end; the app's rounding of the measured twist

ior.note: a place just inspected is ignored for about five seconds, the app's rounding

field.name: squeeze
field.note: the whole circle of sight is pressed into the phone picture

gaze.name: strip
gaze.note: the sharp strip is drawn moving over the picture

gaze.name: stamps
gaze.note: each look is left as a stamp of the sharp picture

rows: A jumping spider has eight eyes in four pairs. The six smaller side eyes between them cover almost the whole circle around the animal, so the picture wraps right round you.

The two big front eyes each see only a strip about 2 degrees wide and 21 degrees tall at a time. Sharpness in that strip reaches about 3.8 cycles a degree in a Phidippus, and the best salticid, Portia, reaches about 12.5. A person reads about 30 cycles a degree on a chart.
Side eyes see coarsely and only movement

The side eyes resolve at best about 1.3 cycles a degree in one species measured. A Metaphidippus behaved as though completely blind to stationary objects, and a light that only went on and off drew no turn at all.

The front eyes carry an ultraviolet pigment near 360 nanometres and a green one near 530. The side eyes carry a single green pigment near 535, so they give no colour. The wide picture is drawn in one tone and the thin front strip carries two colours.

The colour of each eye is built from pigment peaks: 535 nanometres for the side eyes, and 360 and 530 for the front eyes. The speed of a look is worked out from a 15 degree jump finishing within 0.1 second, which gives about 6.7 milliseconds a degree and is an upper bound.
Eyes that move behind fixed lenses

The front retinas sweep side to side across what they inspect, and they also twist to either side and rest at each end. A place just inspected is passed over for a few seconds. The records describe these movements with ranges, and the app rounds them to single numbers of its own.
Side eyes call, front eyes look
Movement seen by the side eyes starts a turn, and then the front eyes take over to look closely at the target. The strip in the picture therefore swings toward whatever moves.

Still things fade by a set amount and do not vanish, because the records say only that the side eyes ignore stillness. Movement that looks alive gets extra weight, since the side eyes can tell walking-like motion from random dots. Ultraviolet in the front strip is drawn from the camera's blue, because phones record almost none and blue contrasts in natural scenes resemble ultraviolet ones.
